name: Salkantay trek to Machu Picchu
why: The wild way to Machu Picchu, no permit needed: over a 4,600 m pass under the Salkantay glacier and down through cloud forest and coffee farms.
book: No permit. Most go with an agency from Cusco (camps or lodges, mules for the bags); book the Machu Picchu entry and the train back separately.
water: Camps boil water; small shops in the villages from day 3.
dangers: The pass at about 4,600 m on day 2: frost at night at Soraypampa.
From hot jungle to snow in 24 hours: layers, not one big coat.
turnaround: If you feel altitude sickness at Soraypampa, take the horse over the pass or go back to Mollepata.

points.name: Soraypampa under Nevado Salkantay
points.note: Day 1: by car from Cusco (or a long day on foot from Mollepata); the coldest night, at 3,900 m. Humantay lake in the afternoon.

points.name: Salkantay Pass
points.note: Day 2: about 4,600 m, stone cairns and the glacier just above; then 800 m down to Huaracmachay.

points.name: Collpapampa and Chaullay
points.note: Night 2: the first warm villages, at about 2,900 m, after a long descent into the green valley.

points.name: La Playa, Santa Teresa valley
points.note: Day 3: down the river through cloud forest, waterfalls, coffee and passion fruit farms.

points.name: Llactapata ruins, Machu Picchu view
points.note: Day 4: 800 m up an old Inca path; from the ruins, Machu Picchu is seen side-on across the valley.

points.name: Aguas Calientes
points.note: Steep down to Hidroeléctrica, then 2.5 hours along the railway; Machu Picchu on day 5.
